title: Local-Time AdamW for Stability-Gap Reduction in Continual Learning

contributions.purpose: Explain a previously underexplored cause of the continual-learning stability gap.
contributions.mechanism: Identify that AdamW's bias correction, designed for zero-initialized (cold-start) moments, becomes counterproductive at task boundaries where moment buffers are warm but stale, so full-strength updates (s(t)~1) are applied to misaligned preconditioning precisely when caution is needed.
contributions.evaluation: Mechanistic argument grounded in the bias-correction scale factor s(t)=sqrt(1-beta2^t)/(1-beta1^t); s(1)~0.316.
contributions.domain: Continual learning / optimizer state at task boundaries
contributions.source_quote: We identify optimizer bias correction as a contributor to the stability gap in continual learning, providing a mechanistic explanation for post-switch instability.

contributions.purpose: Reduce the stability gap with a minimal, drop-in optimizer change.
contributions.mechanism: Local-Time AdamW (LT-AdamW): reset only the bias-correction timestep t to 0 at each task boundary while preserving the moment buffers m and v; this dampens the effective learning rate by ~3x (1/s(1)~3.16) in early post-switch steps, recovering to full strength as moments adapt. One-line PyTorch change.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a hyperparameter-free drop-in replacement.
contributions.source_quote: We propose LT-AdamW, a one-line modification to standard AdamW that resets only the timestep counter at task boundaries.

contributions.mechanism: Evaluate on Rotated MNIST (Domain-IL) and Split CIFAR-100 (Class-IL) with ResNet-18, comparing CarryAll-AdamW, NoBiasCorr, and LT-AdamW over 5 seeds; metrics SG, min-ACC, ACC, BWT.
contributions.domain: Image-classification continual learning (Rotated MNIST, Split CIFAR-100)
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that LT-AdamW reduces the stability gap by 17-31% across two benchmarks (Rotated MNIST and Split CIFAR-100), with improvements in minimum post-switch accuracy of up to 24%.

contributions.purpose: Validate the theoretical mechanism and confirm the effect is specific to the timestep reset.
contributions.mechanism: Measure post-switch parameter update norms vs theoretical 1/s(1); include a NoBiasCorr control that disables bias correction entirely.
contributions.evaluation: Update dampening 3.42-3.65x closely matches theoretical ~3.16; NoBiasCorr does NOT help (Split CIFAR-100 SG 0.519, worse than CarryAll 0.486), confirming the benefit comes specifically from the timestep reset, not any optimizer change.
contributions.source_quote: We validate the mechanism through theoretical analysis and empirical measurements showing that update dampening matches predictions, and confirm specificity via a control experiment that disables bias correction.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Recent work in reinforcement learning has shown that resetting Adam's timestep can address similar non-stationarity issues (Ellis et al., 2024; Asadi et al., 2023), motivating our investigation in the continual learning setting.

In reinforcement learning, Asadi et al. (2023) showed that periodically resetting optimizer state can improve performance, and Ellis et al. (2024) proposed resetting Adam's timestep to address non-stationarity... Our work brings these insights to continual learning, specifically targeting the bias-correction mechanism at task boundaries.
Lange et al. (2022) identified the stability gap phenomenon... However, the role of optimizer state in the stability gap has remained largely unexplored.
AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter, 2017) decouples weight decay from the gradient-based update... Our work examines how this correction interacts with task boundaries in continual learning.

notes: The method is essentially a direct transfer of Ellis et al. (2024)'s 'Adam on local time' timestep-reset idea from RL non-stationarity to continual-learning task boundaries (the paper's own title echoes it). Authors note LT-AdamW does not address fundamental forgetting and benefits are strongest in Class-IL with stronger inter-task interference.
